messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated error rate calling AWS KMS Encrypt/Decrypt in us-east-1. 5xx/504 observed, ~40% p99 latency spike. Generated by KMS-proxy-monitoring.
Lena (oncall): ack. I'm paged, looking now. Any customer-facing impact reported?
Maya (support): seeing a few support tickets about new instances failing to start (500s during bootstrap). Existing sessions seem ok.
Ravi: confirming logs from instance-start-controller show repeated failures during key fetch/unwrap. Error snippet: `kms client error: 504 Gateway Timeout` then `signing_failed: context deadline exceeded`.
Carlos: stack traces point to our node-key-init task timing out after 30s. That's the place where we call KMS to unwrap the data-key.
Lena (oncall): running `kubectl -n infra logs deploy/key-init --since=1h | grep -i kms | tail -n 50` now.
ops-bot: Deploy job infra/key-init v2.3 restarted 12 pods in last 10m due to LivenessProbe failures.
Lena (oncall): TL;DR: KMS API in us-east-1 shows degraded control plane. This is causing node boot workflows to fail when they try to unwrap keys -> new instances hang on startup and return 500s for sign requests.
Ravi: Root cause seems external (AWS KMS). I'm hitting the AWS status page and CloudWatch metrics show increased latency/failure rate for KMS API. No signs of our infra overload.
Carlos: Can we switch to cached-encrypted-keys fallback? We have a local key-cache and we keep wrapped keys in S3 for warm instances. But our code requires unwrap at startup unless `ALLOW_KMS_FALLBACK` is set.
Lena (oncall): Initiating mitigation: 1) flip feature flag `ALLOW_KMS_FALLBACK=true` for node-init to allow using locally cached wrapped keys for boot 2) extend key-init timeout to 90s 3) increase retry/backoff to 5 retries with exponential backoff.
Maya (support): I'll draft a customer message: "We're experiencing delays when starting new instances in us-east-1 due to transient third-party (KMS) errors. Existing requests are unaffected. We're mitigating and will update".
Ravi: patch ready. Command to patch deployment: ```kubectl -n infra set env deploy/key-init ALLOW_KMS_FALLBACK=true && kubectl -n infra set env deploy/key-init KMS_TIMEOUT=90``` Applying now.
Carlos: Also suggest toggling signing client to fail-open for non-critical signing during boot with `SIGNING_FAIL_OPEN=true` so startup doesn't block. That only affects telemetry/signing of telemetry blobs, not customer data ops.
Lena (oncall): Applying both. Running `kubectl rollout restart deploy/key-init` after env changes.
ops-bot: Rollout started for infra/key-init. 0->3 ready.
Lena (oncall): Observing pod logs. New pods are now returning success for key-unwrap using cached wrapped keys. Startup latency back to normal for those nodes.
Maya (support): Updating customers: posted initial note to status with guidance and ETA 30m for mitigation.
Ravi: Monitoring KMS error rate and our retries. Putting an extra circuit-breaker to avoid overwhelming KMS: limit outbound KMS concurrency from 200 -> 40. Patch pushed to infra config map.
Carlos: Note: this will throttle concurrent startups, but avoids amplifying the external outage. We should re-scale rolling updates accordingly.
Lena (oncall): Good catch. I'll coordinate with deploys. Anyone running large canary or infra migrations should pause. Ping me.
Maya (support): Received reply from 2 customers saying they saw instance create failures with error `signing_failed`. I've escalated to account teams for high-touch customers.
ops-bot: Incident page created: https://internal.incidents/1763312345 (auto). Priority: P2 initially, may ramp to P1 if KMS persists.
Ravi: AWS status shows "degradation of service" for KMS in us-east-1; also filing support case ID 987654321.
Carlos: For long-term: propose adding a persistent local key cache for wrapped keys and a startup mode that avoids any remote unwrap for the first 2 minutes. Also better exponential backoff with jitter.
Lena (oncall): Agreed. But short-term: mitigation successful — new nodes starting with fallback. Marking immediate customer-impact mitigated. Monitoring for residual errors.
Maya (support): Updated status: "Mitigation in place — new instances can start using fallback. AWS KMS still reporting issues; we are monitoring. No broader request failures reported at this time".
incidents-bot: :white_check_mark: Post-mitigation check: service KMS call error rate down to 7% from 40% in the last 10m.
Lena (oncall): Handing over to Ravi for follow-up and RCA tomorrow. I'll be off-shift in 10m. Ravi, can you own the post-incident review and timeline?
Ravi: Taking handoff. Will collect logs, add graphs (p99 latency, error rate) and draft RCA. Also will coordinate with AWS support to get root cause timeline and request replay logs.
Lena (oncall): Thanks. Quick runbook notes: - actions taken: flipped ALLOW_KMS_FALLBACK, increased timeouts, limited KMS concurrency - customer comms posted - support case opened with AWS - pause large infra rollouts
Ravi: Noted. I'll also schedule a postmortem sync with infra and SRE. Tentative time: tomorrow 11am.
Maya (support): Sending follow-up to customers: include workaround for users who can pre-warm keys: `prewarm --region us-east-1` and contact support for urgent cases.
Carlos: One more ask: create an alert to fire when KMS unwrap failure rate >10% AND restart rate for key-init pods >5/min. We almost had a cascading restart loop.
Lena (oncall): Created alert rule in Sentry/Alerting.
incidents-bot: Incident status changed -> mitigated. Duration so far: ~28m.
Ravi: I'll keep monitoring for another 2h and will post RCA draft. Thanks all.
Maya (support): Closing support tickets with workaround guidance; leaving high-touch customers open.
Lena (oncall): Leaving channel. Good job team. :team-heart:
